hypothesis: The msgsend ~689-692ms p50 submit_to_settle (unchanged across four prior heads, never decomposed) hides a dominant parity-safe product cost somewhere between submit->ack (0.2ms since #2868), provider request->first token, streaming body, and turn_end->settle (assistant write, session append, UI settle).
approach: BASELINE DECOMPOSITION ONLY, no code changes, no commits on any lane branch. A single-VM (fct6ne9kszq00r72pdk2jlud, 16c/32GB ubuntu:22.04) controlled scripted-turn matrix at origin/rust tip 7064d039a replicates the bench compare.msg_send mock-regime protocol BYTE-EXACTLY (120x40 PTY; probe-input-ready Zq7x walk; erase_all; typed prompt 'bench hello'; Enter; ack = first PTY chunk after Enter; settle = DEFAULT_REPLY[:20] visible in whitespace-normalized screen + 600ms screen-hash stability at 0.02s polls) and adds decomposition instrumentation: exact per-chunk PTY ledger + per-chunk screen digests, session-JSONL row-arrival watcher (2ms poll; row's own ISO timestamps), PI_REQUEST_TIMING=1 (#2852) request-phase entries, per-process CPU/RSS/PSS sampler (100ms), pre/mid/post spin calibration, loadavg. Provider variants (24 trials total, sequential same-VM): http (bench mock_provider.py SSE on 127.0.0.1:8890 + models.json prime-inference/mock-1 + TUI --provider/--model/--offline - the ORIGINAL 690ms evidence's exact provider path), faux-unpaced (PRIME_AGENT_FAUX_SCRIPT engine:faux, in-process, brief-mandated), faux-800 (engine:faux tokensPerSecond=800). 2 warm trials + 4 PI_REQUEST_TIMING-off controls. One strace -f diagnostic trial (not used for timing evidence) to root-cause a ~20ms worker park.
parity_notes: No product edits; nothing merged; frozen parity untouched. Trial protocol fidelity: typed prompt session rows contain exactly 'bench hello' (0 probe-token leftovers across all 24 trials); within-variant session JSONL rows identical modulo ids/timestamps/cwd (rows 1-6 byte-identical per variant); http variant rows carry prime-inference/mock-1, faux variant rows carry the daemon default model (TUI launched without --provider/--model per the streaming-lane pattern) - disclosed protocol difference that does not touch the measured path. Driver/harness files live in /home/ubuntu/hillclimb/fixtures/msgsettle/ (bench repo untouched outside this record).

outcome: discarded (negative result, hypothesis refuted): the ~690ms submit_to_settle is NOT a product cost - ~89% is the compare.msg_send settle protocol's deliberate 600ms screen-stability window plus its 0.02s poll grid (620.6ms p50 from first-stable-poll to settle fire); the visible turn paints in 19-38ms and its largest product-side items are parity-frozen or parity-parity mechanisms (worker coalescer 50ms flush tick; TS-parity auth-lock 20ms retry). No dominant parity-safe edit exists; no code changed.
decision: Close msgsettle NEGATIVE per the brief's no-claim bar. The 690ms is the scripted turn's inherent content (the deliberate settle wait). Reported-only findings for other lanes/orchestrator: (1) fresh-session auth-lock contention ~20ms on http-provider first turns (TS-parity retry; would need a worker-side auth/model-resolution cache to remove - parity-sensitive, ~20ms, not pursued); (2) the settle METRIC itself has a 600ms floor by construction - any future submit_to_settle comparison should treat 690ms as protocol, not product, and the bench msg_send settle detector could optionally be re-specified (harness-only question for the orchestrator, NOT a product change).
